Kim/Marissa/Jonas — forwarding Acme's ask. Procurement wants an operations document we can attach to the DPA that covers:

- Definitions: live data, short-term KV cache, snapshots/snapshots in backups, offsite archival, subprocessor copies
- Standard deletion workflow and timelines (sync to DPA clauses)
- Emergency purge flow (who signs off internally/legal, expected min/max times by data plane)

- Subprocessor visibility and how we notify customers when a backup is in subprocessor custody

Please draft a short runbook (one page + table) and a concise line we can drop into the DPA: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to execute an emergency purge within X-Y hours for live data and within Z days for backups, subject to subprocessor constraints and applicable law."

Jonas — can you check the backup topology and call out where subprocessor custody exists (S3 with vendor X, offsite tape with vendor Y, etc.)?

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-05T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data retention for pilot — Acme asks for emergency purge/runbook

Team — draft below (attached as PDF and updated matrix). I'm keeping the language conservative but customer-friendly. Highlights:

1) Live data (primary store) — emergency purge: RTO 0-6 hours after validated request (validation = signed legal representative + audit ticket). Process: legal triage -> ops exec approval -> blocking of syncs -> purge + verification.
2) Short-term snapshots (hot backups held <7 days) — emergency purge target: 24-72 hours; we must coordinate snapshot tombstone propagation across caches.
3) Long-term backups/archival (cold backups, immutable snapshots, offsite subprocessor) — emergency purge target: 7-30 days depending on subprocessor SLA and jurisdiction. If the backup is under the custody of a subprocessor with a separate retention contract, we escalate to our vendor ops; target timeline communicated in vendor notice.
4) Logs & forensics — by default we retain logs for 90 days. For forensic holds we will pause purge for defined scope; release requires documented legal authorization. We provide a documented exception flow for audit purposes.

Escape hatch (emergency purge override):
- Criteria: court order release / signed customer written request + JIRA ticket + 2 internal approvers (Legal + Ops lead).
- When invoked, we will: (a) freeze replication, (b) coordinate with subprocessor vendors and request their immediate purge, (c) perform verification and provide hash-level evidence when possible.

Attachments: DPA redline line + matrix included. I'm recommending we commit to the following DPA-friendly wording for the "Emergency Purge" clause: 

"Where Customer submits a verified emergency purge request in accordance with the process set forth in the Operations Runbook, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete purge of Live Data within 0-6 hours, Short-term Backups within 24-72 hours, and Long-term Backups within 7-30 days, subject to subprocessor custody and applicable law; Redwood will provide written confirmation and available verification artifacts within five (5) business days."

Notes: Jonas — I flagged two backup locations in the matrix that are under vendor custody (VendorX S3 vault and VendorY archival service). We will need to open vendor-side POA/expedite lanes for Acme pilot.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
